races.title: State House, District 62
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: John M. Blust
cands.bio: Republican attorney and accountant from Guilford County. He holds a B.S. and J.D. from UNC-Chapel Hill and is an Army veteran. He served in the NC House for District 62 from 2001 to 2018, and was appointed to the same seat in September 2024.
cands.gaps: We could not find where John Blust was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no independent news coverage or official records confirming the bills and actions his campaign website describes, including his claims about data-center cost rules, property tax freezes, grocery tax repeal and a foreign-adversary farmland ban. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for his 2024 or 2026 campaigns, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found nothing on his positions on abortion, guns, development, or data-center bans or moratoriums. We also found no controversies or foreign ties.

qual.background: Attorney and accountant who earned his law degree at UNC-Chapel Hill. He served in the NC House for District 62 from 2001 to 2018 and was appointed back to the seat in 2024. He also served in the U.S. Army.
qual.why: He has long prior legislative service in the same chamber and a law and accounting career, both of which fit the work of writing law and the state budget. Committee chair roles were not counted.
qual.label: He has long prior legislative service in the same chamber and a law and accounting career, both of which fit the work of writing law and the state budget. Committee chair roles were not counted.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says he supports exempting the first $100,000 of a home's value from property tax. He also says he championed a freeze on property tax revaluations and supported a constitutional amendment capping how much local governments can raise property taxes.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Says he sponsored legislation banning foreign adversaries such as China from buying farmland in North Carolina.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he worked to secure the largest teacher pay raise in 20 years and supports providing opportunity to all students regardless of their parents' income.

workers-first.evidence: His 2016 campaign website listed securing the border and controlling immigration as a theme, including tracking and preventing visa overstays and building the wall.

cands.name: Shelly Headen
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for NC House District 62 from Oak Ridge, Guilford County. Appalachian State graduate (1991). Former auditor at an international CPA firm, pharmaceutical company accounting manager and accounting recruiter. Now a small business owner in construction and garage doors. Has held no elected office.

controversies.text: In September 2026, older social media posts under Headen's name resurfaced. They included wishing for an attack on US soil in Alabama and Louisiana and "Ready for the MAGAs to die off!!" The House Democratic Caucus and Guilford County Democrats withdrew support. Headen said she recalled writing anti-Trump posts but not their wording, and didn't remember the Alabama comment.

endorsements.text: Work For Democracy (listed by Headen in her Ballotpedia survey and on Ballotpedia's endorsement list)
Center for Freethought Equality (listed on Ballotpedia's endorsement list). The Guilford County Democratic Party and NC House Democratic Caucus later withdrew their support.

cands.gaps: We could not find a town of birth, the year she moved to Guilford County, or any record of her holding public office. Her statements on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration and H-1B, policing, guns and abortion were not found. Her site calls for fully funding public schools and paying teachers more but says nothing on vouchers, charters or school choice. Her campaign site says 'as a CPA', but we found no license record, and her biography describes her work as an auditor at a CPA firm. Original reporting on the social media posts (The Assembly, WFDD) was not available to read.
